# collector corpus verification — resolution transition
#
# ambiguous_groups: CLOSED, exactly one of the N targets is correct.
# dynamic_groups: OPEN, dispatches to one of these or beyond.
# THE TWO ARE NEVER SUMMED. A reader who adds them has reported a
# language property (runtime dispatch) as an index gap (ambiguity).
# dynamic_unbound counts dynamic references whose scope declares nothing
# by that name: no edge, no group — the largest population of all.
# dot_scope_binds / dot_scope_groups are RESOLUTION residue, not a census
# of the construct: a corpus can carry dot imports that bind nothing, and
# those are counted by the binds pass under dot_scopes_filled instead.
# test_calls_edges is what the chunker EMITTED as TEST_CALLS;
# test_calls_test_to_production is the resolved subset whose target is not
# test code. They are their own counters, added to no row above — but they
# do NOT make the rows above production-only. Every reference row counts
# each edge that is neither CONTAINS nor IMPORTS, and TEST_CALLS rides the
# same resolution walk CALLS does, so bound / external_references and the
# per-language rows of any language with a TestBlocks query count
# test-origin references beside production ones. Read them as ALL
# references. The 18 languages with no TestBlocks query emit no TEST_CALLS
# at all, which is why the go_ rows did not move when this row pair landed.
#

#
# go_binds_files / go_binds_entries are the LIVENESS control: zero here
# means the arm never ran, which reads as "no improvement" without them.
# go_binds_scopes_unknown is the input the external-qualifier rung consumes.
# go_external and go_r2x_terminations are RECORDED, NOT GATED: terminating
# a reference that previously became a wrong dynamic edge RAISES external,
# so a gate demanding it fall would be demanding the defect back.
# go_ambiguous_group_<n> lines list each surviving group's key and the file
# of every candidate — the input to the manual attribution criterion.
#
# ATTRIBUTION OF THE SURVIVING GROUPS, recorded here rather than in the
# artifact body because the artifact is generated and a hand-edit would be
# erased by the next regeneration. Every group listed below was checked by
# reading the //go:build line of each candidate file, and all of them are
# MUTUALLY-EXCLUSIVE BUILD-CONSTRAINT PAIRS — several declarations of one
# name in one scope, which is the ticket's stated legitimately-ambiguous
# class and the correct answer rather than residue to drive to zero. The
# three families seen are: GOOS pairs (a _linux.go file against a _stub.go
# carrying //go:build !linux), //go:build devendpoint against !devendpoint,
# and //go:build internal against !internal.
# A GROUP WHOSE CANDIDATES ARE NOT SUCH A SET IS A DEFECT TO REPORT, never
# residue to accept — re-run this attribution when the listing changes.
